Despite many accounts reporting otherwise, this update has NOT begun rolling out to Tesla customer-owned vehicles.

A single vehicle was detected, and no further rollout has occurred. No Early Access Program participant nor "OG" tester has received this specific build.


Teslascope (@teslascope)

While this might be a real release, there is no evidence at this time that it includes Full Self-Driving V14.3.

We remain vigilant.

We've confirmed that this update does not include Full Self-Driving V14.3.

We'll be keeping an eye out for the first software update to include V14.3 this weekend and throughout next week.

Exclusive: Tesla has included strings in its Robotaxi User Agent, which can be used to track updates to its underlying infotainment software builds.

Most recently, the build was: feature-robotaxi-2-71-5c2280d61e

Days prior, the string was: feature-robotaxi-1-L4-40-7e197188b4

Our service will automatically publish a post on X once any new software update is detected across tens of thousands of vehicles. This includes automatically parsing release notes.

We remain eager and excited for the much-anticipated Full Self-Driving V14.3 release.

Unlike other software releases on the specific third-party app, this update never parsed release notes and shows zero vehicles.

This implies that the version was either manually added to the service or the update was pulled from the vehicle before it had a chance to install it.

A specific build, 2026.2.9.5, was spotted on another third-party service. However, the circumstances of its appearance are questionable.

While this might be a real release, there is no evidence at this time that it includes Full Self-Driving V14.3.

We remain vigilant.

Tesla has issued an official statement to vehicle owners in South Korea regarding recent unauthorized devices that enable Full Self-Driving in the region.

Tesla reiterates that the use of such devices means you are entirely liable (in every respect) for any incident that occurs due to the device. This closely matches the expectations in regions where Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is available, such as North America and Australia.

The company has also mentioned that, in the region, the usage of these devices may violate local law and that usage is at your own risk.

As with other modifications and devices over the years (across all regions), Tesla has also noted that it reserves the right to refuse warranty repairs, regardless of whether these devices cause the damage.

These devices have been used in many other countries outside South Korea. However, we’ve not been made aware of any emails or other communications from the company at this time.
